newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF urges next Nomura president to restore trust.
newsitem.headline: MOF urges next Nomura president to restore trust.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday he had urged the next president of scandal-tainted Nomura Securities Co Ltd to make utmost efforts to restore market confidence when they met earlier in the day.
Mitsuzuka told reporters that Nomura's next president, Junichi Ujiie, currently a managing director, and current president and chairman Masashi Suzuki visited the ministry.
"I told them that as a leading company Nomura should make utmost efforts to win confidence," Mitsuzuka said.
He said he also called on the two executives to cooperate in an investigation being conducted by prosecutors and the securities watchdog to regain investors' trust.

On Tuesday, Nomura announced plans for a drastic reshuffle of the firm's top management. The announcement said Suzuki will resign as president, Ujiie will replace Suzuki and 15 other board members will step down.
